Overview
This video features Twitch streamer xQc reacting to police bodycam and tactical footage from a bizarre and extreme standoff in Volusia County, Florida. What began as a petty theft of three packs of cigarettes escalated into a shootout, an arson attempt, and the deployment of heavy tactical equipment.

The Standoff and Shootout
The incident begins when 56-year-old Dempsey Hadley, seemingly under the influence of drugs, steals cigarettes from an area where he was a known customer [00:14]. Police track him to his residence and attempt a felony traffic stop while he is still in his car in the driveway [00:56].

When officers approach the vehicle with a ballistic shield and attempt to break the window, Hadley opens fire, grazing one deputy (Ethan Thomas) in the face [02:13] and nearly hitting a sergeant. Hadley then refuses to exit his vehicle, lighting items inside the car on fire [04:46]. He bizarrely claims that he was "pardoned by Joe Biden" [05:06].

Escalation to the House
Hadley eventually exits the burning car and runs into his house, leading to an hours-long standoff [08:12]. Officers deploy impact rounds, tear gas, and pepper balls into the home to force his surrender [09:52].

Hadley attempts to set his house on fire while climbing into the attic and subsequently falling through the roof/ceiling [09:10]. The police eventually deploy heavy armored vehicles, including a BearCat and a specialized tactical breaching vehicle called "The Rook," which uses a hydraulic lift to reach the second-story balcony [13:30].

Arrest and Sentencing
As the house fills with smoke and fire, Hadley is forced out onto the balcony, where heavily armored officers on the lift secure him with zip ties [15:42]. As he is being treated, he casually remarks, "I don't think he's [Biden] going to pardon me after this" [16:58].

Hadley was charged with three counts of attempted first-degree murder of a law enforcement officer, fleeing/eluding, and petty theft [17:35]. After two years in jail, he took a plea deal and was sentenced to 11 years in prison, followed by 10 years of supervised release [18:01]. Streamer xQc expresses disbelief at the relatively short sentence, arguing that a deliberate attempt to kill police officers should carry a much harsher penalty [18:30].

A tax deduction doesn’t make you money. It reduces taxable income. If you donate $10 million, you don’t get $10 million back. There is no universe where giving away more money somehow increases your wealth through taxes. That’s not how math works. To profit from a deduction, you’d need the government to reimburse you more than you gave. That simply does not happen. At best, you soften the financial hit.

And even if someone did get a deduction, the money still built all of these schools. The public benefit doesn’t disappear because the tax code recognizes charitable giving.

Calling large-scale philanthropy a “tax write-off scheme” is just a complete misunderstanding of basic accounting.

Avgeek here: anyone that has questions feel free to ask me. UPS 2976 was a regular scheduled flight from Kentucky to Honolulu. This means that the plane was loaded with over 100,000 LB of fuel, nearly a full load. a cracked engine mount, caused the engine #1, the left wing-mounted engine to detach by flying over the top of the wing. All airliners since the 1970s are certified to takeoff and climb with one engine loss, whether its a quad jet, trijet, or a 2 jet aircraft, they're meant to fly without an engine. In this case, The plane allegedly tore off some of the slats/flaps that are deployed for takeoff, which are meant to create more lift at slower speeds. when this tore off, several factors occurred. Asymmetric drag, asymmetric thrust and asymmetric lift. This caused the plane to bank left slightly, which eventually caused the plane to crash. A relatable incident is American Airlines flight 191- a nearly identical crash back in 1977 on the same type of aircraft.

If you’re going for a "Felix" (xQc) inspired fursuit nose, we aren't just making a standard dog button. We are talking about the legendary "schnozer"—a nose with a prominent bridge, a bit of a "beak" profile, and significant character.
Here is how to sculpt and assemble a custom fursuit nose that captures that specific look.
1. Sculpt the Foam Base
The "xQc look" is all about the profile. You want to move away from a flat animal nose and toward something with a defined bridge.
 * Material: Use high-density upholstery foam (green or white).
 * The Shape: Carve a "T" shape where the top of the T is the bridge of the nose and the bottom is the tip.
 * The Bridge: Make the bridge higher and narrower than a standard canine nose. It should start between the eyes and slope down.
 * The Tip: Instead of a round ball, give it a slightly "droopy" or pointed tip to mimic the iconic silhouette.
2. Refining the Nostrils
To make it look like a "furry" version of a human feature, the nostrils need to be stylized.
 * Use a hobby knife (X-Acto) to hollow out two deep, teardrop-shaped nostrils on the underside.
 * Ensure the "septum" (the bit between the nostrils) is thin but sturdy.
3. Patterning (The Tape Method)
Once your foam sculpt looks like a masterpiece of a schnozer, you need to turn that 3D shape into a 2D fabric pattern.
 * Wrap it: Cover the foam nose tightly in saran wrap, then cover that in duct tape.
 * Draw your lines: Use a Sharpie to draw a line down the center (symmetry is key!) and a line where the nose will meet the fur of the muzzle.
 * Cut it off: Carefully cut the tape off. If it doesn't lay flat on a table, make small "dart" cuts (V-shapes) until it does.
4. Choose Your "Skin"
The material determines the vibe of the suit.
 * Minky: The gold standard. It’s soft, slightly fuzzy, and hides seams well.
 * Vinyl/Pleather: If you want a "wet" or realistic look.
 * Fleece: Good for a "toony" or matte look.
5. Assembly
 * Sewing: Trace your tape patterns onto the fabric (leave a 5mm seam allowance). Sew the pieces together, usually starting from the tip and working back toward the bridge.
 * The "Stuffing": You can either glue the fabric directly onto your foam sculpt using high-temp hot glue, or "skin" it over the foam like a sock.
 * The Nostrils: Tuck the fabric into the hollowed-out nostril holes and glue it down inside for a clean, seamless look.
6. Final Details
To really sell the look, add some "juice":
 * Airbrushing: Use a slightly darker shade (brown or dark pink) around the nostrils and the bridge to give it depth.
 * Highlight: A tiny dab of white acrylic paint or "Liquitex Gloss Medium" on the bridge of the nose can make it look like it's catching the light (and make it look bigger).
Comparison: Standard vs. "Schnozer" Nose
| Feature | Standard Canine Nose | xQc-Style Nose |
|---|---|---|
| Bridge Height | Low / Flat | High / Defined |
| Tip Shape | Round / Heart-shaped | Tapered / Pointed |
| Placement | Low on the muzzle | Extends up toward the eyes |
| Nostril Style | Wide / Circular | Deep / Elongated |
> Pro Tip: If you want the nose to be "boopable" but still hold its specific shape, use EVA foam for the internal structure and wrap it in a thin layer of soft foam before adding the fabric. This keeps the bridge from collapsing!

In Canada, driving under the influence (DUI) causing death isn't always charged as murder; instead, it often falls under Impaired Driving Causing Death, a serious offense with severe penalties (min 4 yrs, max life imprisonment). If circumstances show extreme recklessness or intent, prosecutors might pursue Manslaughter, carrying broader sentencing discretion, often resulting in 10-15+ years.

In the U.S., driving under the influence (DUI) that causes someone's death can lead to charges like vehicular manslaughter, a form of involuntary manslaughter, where the driver unintentionally kills someone while committing another unlawful act (drunk driving). These charges, often called DUI manslaughter or vehicular homicide, require proving impairment and causation, carrying severe penalties like lengthy prison time (up to 20 years or more), hefty fines, and license revocation, varying by state.

In order to photograph the sun like shown with the sky diver one it’s just a goddamn filter you need to put in front of a telescope in order to see the solar flares, it’s just a filter.

And as for other astro images, if you really want to go the hard way you can use a ccd camera, narrowband filters and what not, but you can just simply use your regular camera for it and you don’t need to take different wavelengths of color, separately, but what the video doesn’t explain to noobs and clueless idiots is that the further or dimmer an object is, the more time of exposure is needed in order to capture all the details, it’s not instantaneous like taking a fking snap shot of a tree in a park, these things are mostly gases, it’s like smoke, insanely huge clouds of dust hanging there, and they change overtime of course, but it takes decades to see the slightest changes, and either way what you need is what’s called an equatorial mount, which is like a tripod that follows the rotation of the earth/or sky depending on what you believe or think, and this mount enables you to track a selected target, and take as many 30-1 minute exposures, that you then need to stack together in order to reveal all the details.

See if you want to image like the famous pillars of creation, which is called a nebulae, you need at least about 1 hour worth of exposures in order to create a decent picture of it, like I said it’s not instantaneous, and this is because the nebulae is very far from us, and light “travels” to reach us, so in order to see these objects in the sky the photons (the visible light) takes time to reach us, again, it’s not as easy to see as just opening your eyes and seeing the tree or something like it is on earth, there is no easy way to explain it other than to say that the image and its details need to travel to your eyes, but even then, you need to accumulate the light in order to have it fully revealed and that’s why people don’t even realise, but Hubble or Webb images are actually days and sometimes even weeks worth of exposures, people have no idea.

And with that said, nasa takes it to the extreme by using all sorts of filters in order to reveal all sorts of additional components which are hidden to a normal sensor, they indeed capture more than hydrogen alpha (the primary gas of nebulae) which is pink/red, they also capture sulfur oxygen 3 and more, but you can see the pillars of creation with a normal dslr, which basically shows you reality as you would see it with your eyes, and all these objects actually look pink/red, they don’t look creamy brown with deep blues and what not.

Anyways, for having done astrophotography for a number of years, I can tell you that much that I know pretty much everything there is to know about the subject, and that narrowband imaging is really a kind of interpretation to make these nebulae look better than they look with human eyes in terms of colors, but no one believing that the earth is flat thinks these objects are fake or made up, it just takes time and effort to get to the bottom on how to image these things, but you don’t need to be a Einstein for it, it’s actually stupidly easy to do and even after years of studying the subject on my own I wouldn’t put my life on the line telling you that the earth is a sphere in space revolving around the sun and travelling at lightning speed through space, simply because aside from very minor changes in the clouds of nebulae, there are no changes in the sky as to the positioning of stars and constellations, the night sky never truly changes, and common sense even tells you that it’s the things in the sky that are revolving around us, not us around them.

If you’re interested, you can check out my astrophotography account on instagram @yucitastro and prove that I’m legit and that I know what I’m talking about

The script was originally written for a live action TV show and it's budget is limited. Hopefully with the financial success of the 
game they will make a second season and improve upon it. This style isn't for everyone and if you didn't enjoy it as much as the others
it valid but there is clearly a market for games like this. 

The positives:
Good character designs, characters that resonated with people, entertaining story. The choice the player base cares about the most were the romance option between Invisigal or Blonde Blazer. Casting content creators was a smart idea. It's basically free promotion. There were definitely some funny jokes in the game. Jacksepticye, Penguinz0, and Joel Haver did a great job despite not being professional voice actors. 

Criticisms/Improvements:
Obviously there are valid criticisms. There are audio issues like inconsistent audio for the characters. Some characters have a lower audio than others. Probably because they were filmed in different locations. Not of the jokes landed but some of them did. xQc clearly found some of these jokes to be funny as well. It's a bit cliche at certain moments. The Game play section could also use more variety as it's limited to only 2 types (if you exclude the dialogue choices). The episodes are too short usually with the format of 1. Cut scene/dialogue 2. Game play section 3. Cut scene/dialogue 4. Game play section 5. Cut scene, usually lasting around an hour. Could use more cut scene/dialogue for more character development and fleshing out the world. People clearly want to spend more time with these characters and explore the world they've built. 8 episodes is a bit too short perhaps 10 episodes if they are making a season 2. 

Considering the developmental challenges they've faced and a limited budget the developers did a great job. At the end of the day the most important thing is that it's entertaining and clearly a lot of people thought it was entertaining. Hopefully if there is a season 2 the players get to explore and see more of the world they've built and spend more times with the characters.

12:10 I think the hint is in the ad where she says, “Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair color, personality, and even eye color. My genes are blue”. The voiceover then follows with, “Sydney Sweeney has great genes”.

In the ad, they highlight only one specific trait - her blue eyes - and immediately link that to the statement that she has “great genes”. That would imply that blue eyes are somehow a marker of having “great” genes. So, does that mean brown eyes are less great? If yes, the problem is immediately obvious. If not, and all eye colors are equal in an objective sense, then the statement loses its contrastive meaning -  there would be no distinction between “average” and “great.”. In that case, using eye color alone to make such a claim would be meaningless, like saying, “This guy has a head; therefore, he has great genes”.

I’d agree with your take if they had simply said she has “great genes” in a general sense. Many people find her conventionally attractive, and she doesn’t have any visible disabilities or genetic conditions. But that’s not what they emphasized. They chose to focus specifically on eye color, rather than on a trait in which she clearly excels compared to most people. For example, you could say LeBron James has great genes - he’s probably in the top 0.000001% for athleticism.

The difference in viewpoints on this ad comes down to interpretation: do you think there’s a subtle “dog whistle” where “great genes” are attributed to blue eyes, or do you think that those were just two completely separate sentences? Both readings are possible - but to claim there was no hint at all is, in my view, disingenuous and uncharitable to those who think that actually those statements are linked.
